title: Governor of Wyoming

context.text: Open seat: Gov. Mark Gordon (R) is term-limited. In the August 18, 2026 Republican primary, state Sen. Eric Barlow won with 45.1%, defeating Superintendent of Public Instruction Megan Degenfelder, who was endorsed by President Trump, and Brent Bien, who was backed by the Wyoming Republican Party.

Kenneth Casner was unopposed for the Democratic nomination. Rebecca Bextel is the Constitution Party's candidate. The Wyoming Secretary of State's general-election candidate roster (September 9, 2026) lists these three as the only governor candidates.

candidates.name: Eric Barlow
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 2026 Republican primary with 45.1%. Wyoming's gubernatorial ticket does not include a ballot-line running mate; the governor runs alone and the secretary of state is next in line.
candidates.currentRole: Wyoming state senator (since 2023); former Speaker of the Wyoming House

summary.text: Eric Barlow is a Republican state senator from Gillette, a Marine Corps veteran, large-animal veterinarian and rancher. He served in the Wyoming House from 2013 to 2023, including as Speaker in 2021–2022, and chairs the Senate Labor, Health and Social Services Committee. His platform emphasizes cash-based budgeting, healthcare access and public lands.

background.text: Fourth-generation Wyomingite raised on his family's ranch in Campbell County; U.S. Marine Corps veteran; D.V.M. from Colorado State University.
Served in the Wyoming House (District 3) from 2013 to 2023, including as Majority Leader (2019–2021) and Speaker (2021–2023).
Elected to the Wyoming Senate in 2022; chairs the Senate Labor, Health and Social Services Committee.

priorities.text: Cash-based budgeting and 'right-sized government' to avoid boom-bust cycles.
priorities.quote: Cash-based budgeting forces us to set priorities with the money we have today, and not fall victim to boom-bust cycles.

priorities.text: Healthcare access: attract more providers, strengthen rural hospitals and clinics, support EMS, expand behavioral health capacity and improve telehealth.
Does not support a wholesale sale of Wyoming's public lands; has proposed regional governor's offices around the state.
priorities.quote: I do not support the wholesale, fire sale of Wyoming’s public lands.

record.text: Voted yes on SF 101, amendments to the Second Amendment Protection Act, which passed the Senate 26–5 on February 19, 2026; the governor vetoed it.
Voted no on the Senate motion to override the governor's veto of SF 101; the override failed 12–18.
Voted yes on HB 178, which prohibits public employers and specified organizations from automatic deductions of dues and uniform assessments, as specified; it passed the Senate on third reading 21–10.

Voted yes on SJ 5, a joint resolution requesting Congress to call a convention for proposing constitutional amendments; it passed the Senate 19–12 and later failed in the House Committee of the Whole.

Voted yes on SJ 9, a joint resolution requesting that Congress recognize the protection of Wyoming's freedom of access to public lands and local participation in land-management decisions; it passed the Senate 27–4. Barlow is its sponsor.

candidates.name: Kenneth R. Casner
candidates.ballotNote: Unopposed in the August 2026 Democratic primary (10,706 votes).

summary.text: Kenneth Casner is the Democratic nominee for governor and lists an Elk Mountain address. He previously ran for governor in 2002 and 2018. He did not respond to WyoFile's candidate questionnaire, and little public information about his platform was found.

priorities.text: Free and open elections, which he calls his number one issue.
priorities.quote: My number one issue is free and open elections.
You put universal healthcare into Wyoming, and true Wyoming universal healthcare
Number one is you need to restructure your taxes
the one industry I would like to see grow is our small business.

positions.summary: In a Wyoming Public Media interview, said universal health care would have a large effect in Wyoming.
positions.quote: Health, universal healthcare. You put universal healthcare into Wyoming, and true Wyoming universal healthcare, you're gonna see a shock that is unreal.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website found (he posts on Facebook). He did not answer WyoFile's questionnaire; the positions and priorities here come from his Oct. 9, 2026 Wyoming Public Media interview. Not found: statements on abortion, guns, immigration, climate or other guide issues.

candidates.name: Rebecca Bextel

summary.text: Rebecca Bextel is the Constitution Party's candidate for governor, a small business owner who has lived in Wyoming for more than 20 years. She describes herself as a conservative choice and has focused on government accountability, energy, state sovereignty and gun and parental rights.

background.text: Born in Alabama to missionary parents; has lived in Wyoming for more than 20 years, built a small business there and raised four daughters.

priorities.text: Withdraw Wyoming from the federal refugee resettlement program and end driver's licenses for people in the country illegally.
Unleash Wyoming energy and defend Wyoming's water rights and public-land access.
Audit grants, subsidized loans and economic development programs, and find $13 million to move families off the three-year Medicaid waiver wait list.

positions.summary: Campaign site says she will oppose gun-control mandates, firearm registries and red-flag laws.
positions.quote: She will oppose unconstitutional gun-control mandates, firearm registries, red-flag laws that deny due process, and federal efforts to restrict the rights of responsible citizens.

statements.quote: I would find the 13M dollars to move families off the 3 year wait list for the medicaid waiver program.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions and statements come from her campaign issues page and her WyoFile questionnaire answers. Her site's immigration language (driver's licenses, refugee resettlement) and the questionnaire line 'I will enforce the laws of the land' do not squarely address deportations, so they are not shown as a position; 'protecting innocent life' on the site does not name abortion.

researchNotes: The Wyoming Secretary of State's General Election Candidate Roster (generated September 9, 2026) lists exactly three governor candidates: Eric Barlow (Republican), Kenneth R. Casner (Democratic) and Rebecca Bextel (Constitution); this matches the guide, and Joseph Kibler (withdrawn) is not on it. Ballotpedia was unreachable (bot challenge). Barlow's votes were checked against the Wyoming Legislature's official bill-information API (wyoleg.gov) as well as the repo's 2026 Wyoming Senate roll-call snapshot; earlier sessions were not reviewed. Casner did not answer WyoFile's questionnaire and has no campaign website that was found, so his profile is thin; his occupation could not be sourced and was removed. Wyoming governor candidates run alone on the ballot (no running-mate field). Bextel is labeled minimal because she is a minor-party candidate, though her own materials were available.
